cs_elements.name: HSM for OTA Signing Keys
cs_elements.notes: Off-board HSM for OTA firmware signing key lifecycle (generation, rotation, destruction)

cs_elements.name: Secure Element (CryptoAuthLib)
cs_elements.certification: ECC Private Key Storage, AES CCM
cs_elements.algorithms: ECDSA P-256, AES-128 CCM, SHA-256, HMAC
cs_elements.notes: On-board secure element for session key derivation, provisioning, attestation

cs_elements.name: SHE (Secure Hardware Extension) in MCU
cs_elements.algorithms: AES-128 ECB, Key derivation, Anti-rollback counter
cs_elements.notes: Immutable bootloader verification, anti-rollback via monotonic counter, SHE-EXTEND for attestation

cs_elements.name: TLS 1.3 Stack (mbed TLS)
cs_elements.algorithms: AES-256-GCM, ECDH P-256, ECDSA P-384, SHA-384
cs_elements.notes: Mutual TLS 1.3 for OTA download channel, certificate pinning enforced

cs_elements.name: SecOC Implementation (CAN FD)
cs_elements.notes: Message-level authentication for safety-critical CAN frames (steering, braking)

cs_elements.name: Debug Port Disable via Secure Boot
cs_elements.notes: Production firmware disables JTAG/SWD; one-time unlock via HMAC challenge (24-hour validity)

cs_elements.name: Certificate Authority (PKI)
cs_elements.part_number: Intermediate CA for OTA + TLS Server
cs_elements.node: OTA Backend (offline for OTA CA, online for TLS)
cs_elements.notes: Dual CAs: OTA firmware signing (offline, HSM-backed) and TLS server (online for mutual auth)

crypto_operations.rotation_policy: Annual rotation, new cert issued 30 days prior to expiry
crypto_operations.notes: Long-term key (multi-year lifecycle), used to sign all firmware releases

crypto_operations.gen_method: Derived via HKDF-SHA256 from TLS 1.3 handshake PRF
crypto_operations.storage_location: Ephemeral (RAM), zeroized after TLS session close
crypto_operations.notes: AEAD mode provides both confidentiality and integrity; nonce managed by TLS record layer

crypto_operations.gen_method: Generated fresh per TLS handshake by mbed TLS
crypto_operations.notes: Perfect Forward Secrecy (PFS) ensured by ephemeral ECDH; no long-term shared secret
Used in secure boot chain (ROM → Bootloader → App) and TLS 1.3 handshake (PRF)

crypto_operations.gen_method: Derived via AES-KW key derivation from SecOC root key
crypto_operations.storage_location: Secure flash partition (encrypted, fused), or Secure Element if supported
crypto_operations.notes: Per-ECU key; MAC appended to CAN FD data field; freshness counter prevents replay

crypto_operations.purpose: TLS Server Certificate Signing (mutual auth), Device Attestation
crypto_operations.gen_method: Generated in Secure Element (ATECC608A) or provisioned at manufacturing
crypto_operations.storage_location: Secure Element (ATECC608A) or TPM, never extracted
crypto_operations.rotation_policy: Per-device (same key for device lifetime, signed into certificate)
crypto_operations.notes: Used for device identity in mutual TLS; private key never leaves Secure Element

keys.purpose: Sign all OTA firmware releases for ESC ECUs
keys.rotation_policy: Annual rotation; new key generated 90 days before expiry. Old key archived for 5 years.
keys.access_control: Dual-person control: Security Manager + OTA Team Lead (2-of-2 quorum)
keys.destruction_method: Cryptographic zeroization via HSM secure erase command; certificate revocation via CRL

keys.purpose: Derive per-ECU CMAC keys for CAN message authentication (SecOC)
keys.gen_method: Generated in HSM or offline KMS; unique per hardware variant
keys.storage_location: Encrypted flash partition (AES-256 key encryption key)
keys.rotation_policy: Per-firmware version; all ECUs re-keyed on OTA install. Legacy keys archived 12 months.
keys.destruction_method: Overwrite with random data 3x (Gutmann method); audit log signed and timestamped

keys.purpose: Verify Bootloader signature in ROM (SHE boot process)
keys.gen_method: Public key: derived from private key in HSM. Private key held offline.
keys.storage_location: Immutable ROM (Secure Boot ROM), fused into MCU at manufacturing
keys.rotation_policy: No rotation (lifetime of hardware platform). Key embedded in ROM; rollover via MCU redesign.
keys.access_control: Manufacturing line only (programming fuse via JTAG during production)

keys.purpose: Sign device identity and firmware measurement quotes (attestation)
keys.gen_method: Provisioned per-device at manufacturing (generated in Secure Element or offline, imported)
keys.storage_location: ATECC608A Secure Element (CryptoAuthLib slot, never extracted)
keys.rotation_policy: No rotation (per-device for device lifetime). Cert valid ~10 years.
keys.access_control: Attestation verifier (OTA backend service) verifies signature via pinned AIK (Attestation Identity Key) cert
keys.destruction_method: Secure Element factory reset (rare); key remains in SE unless hardware physically destroyed

keys.gen_method: CSR generated in Secure Element or HSM; CA signs certificate; private key never leaves device
keys.rotation_policy: Annual certificate renewal; private key remains stable (same for device lifetime)
keys.access_control: TLS stack (mbed TLS) uses key for TLS handshake only; access controlled by Secure Element
keys.destruction_method: Secure Element factory reset (rare); key cannot be extracted or copied

boot_stages.name: BootROM (OEM-signed)
boot_stages.measured: Yes, into PCR-0 (Secure Boot ROM) via SHA-384
boot_stages.key_location: OEM public key (RSA-2048) fused in ROM during manufacturing
boot_stages.anti_rollback: Monotonic counter: BootROM version counter incremented on each Bootloader update; ROM rejects older versions
boot_stages.secure_unlock: One-time HMAC-SHA256 unlock token (HWID || timestamp); 24-hour validity; backend verifies via PKI
boot_stages.notes: Immutable ROM; cryptographic verification of Bootloader signature before execution

boot_stages.name: Bootloader (OEM-signed, updatable)
boot_stages.key_location: Second-stage public key (RSA-2048 or ECDSA P-256) in BootROM
boot_stages.anti_rollback: Version counter: stored in secure flash or OTP fuse. Bootloader rejected if version < current.
boot_stages.secure_unlock: Debug unlock only via provisioning (manufacturing); production blocks debug by default
boot_stages.notes: Verifies Application signature before boot; measures Application into PCR-2; enforces debug-disable in production

boot_stages.name: Application (OTA-signed, firmware image)
boot_stages.key_location: OTA public key (RSA-4096 or ECDSA P-384) provisioned via initial OTA or manufacturing
boot_stages.anti_rollback: OTA image version counter: checked by Bootloader. Monotonic counter in secure NVM incremented on successful boot.
boot_stages.secure_unlock: N/A (user-facing application, no debug expected in production)
boot_stages.notes: Implements SecOC for CAN, TLS 1.3 for OTA downstream, attestation reporting

secure_channels.auth_method: Mutual certificate authentication (device cert + backend server cert)
secure_channels.replay_protection: TLS record sequence number (implicit in TLS 1.3)
secure_channels.notes: Primary channel for firmware OTA download. Certificate pinning enforced (issuer cert hash pinned in firmware).

secure_channels.protocol: DAP-Link (Cortex Debug Access Port) with Debug Authentication
secure_channels.auth_method: Secure boot enforces debug-disable in production; one-time unlock token only in dev/mfg
secure_channels.notes: Disabled in production firmware. Unlocked only via provisioning challenge-response (HMAC-SHA256).

secure_channels.replay_protection: Freshness value: monotonic counter (SecOC) per message type
secure_channels.notes: Safety-critical messages (steering angle, braking) require SecOC. MAC appended to CAN data; receiver validates.
Query firmware version, release notes, and attestation verification. Separate certificate pinning from firmware download.

access_control_roles.name: OEM Security Team
access_control_roles.privileges: HSM key management (rotation, destruction), certificate issuance, OTA deployment approval
access_control_roles.auth_factors: Multi-factor: PKI certificate + TOTP (time-based OTP) + SMS confirmation
access_control_roles.audit_logging: All operations logged: timestamp, signer identity, operation type, approval chain
access_control_roles.notes: Access to OTA root signing key; highest privilege level

access_control_roles.name: OTA Provisioning Team
access_control_roles.privileges: Firmware signing (using HSM via approved workflow), OTA deployment to fleet
access_control_roles.audit_logging: All firmware sign operations logged; deployment audit trail per ECU/VIN
access_control_roles.privilege_escalation: Cannot escalate; requires OEM Security Team approval for key rotation
access_control_roles.notes: No direct HSM access; uses HSM via approved API (e.g., thales_hsm_client wrapper)

access_control_roles.name: Manufacturing/Field Service Technician
access_control_roles.privileges: Read diagnostic data, one-time device unlock (via provisioning), log collection
access_control_roles.auth_factors: Service badge ID + PIN + Technician certificate (auto-issued, short-lived)
access_control_roles.audit_logging: All unlock and diagnostic operations logged; linked to technician ID and timestamp
access_control_roles.privilege_escalation: No escalation (read-only for diagnostics, unlock only via backend approval)
access_control_roles.notes: Access limited to debugging tools; cannot modify firmware or keys

access_control_roles.name: End-User / Vehicle Owner
access_control_roles.privileges: Initiate OTA (automatic), view update status, perform factory reset (via dealer only)
access_control_roles.auth_factors: Vehicle unlock (NFC/BLE key fob or owner app)
access_control_roles.audit_logging: OTA events logged server-side (version, timestamp, result)
access_control_roles.privilege_escalation: No escalation possible (no user-facing HSM or key access)
access_control_roles.notes: No direct control; OTA fully automated by backend; user cannot downgrade firmware

defense_vectors.layer1: Firewall: Destination IP/port pinning to OTA backend; block unauthorized TLS connections
defense_vectors.layer2: TLS 1.3: Mutual certificate authentication; HSTS enforced; certificate pinning (issuer cert hash)
defense_vectors.layer3: Secure boot: Bootloader verifies firmware signature (RSA-4096 or ECDSA P-384) before execution
defense_vectors.layer4: Anti-rollback: Monotonic counter prevents downgrade to older (possibly vulnerable) firmware
defense_vectors.layer5: Secure storage: Firmware encrypted in flash via XTS-AES (optional); signature verification prevents tampering
defense_vectors.coverage: Multi-layer (TLS + crypto verification + anti-rollback) ensures injection resistance
defense_vectors.notes: TARA-4 threat (critical); requires HSM-backed key; annual key rotation

defense_vectors.attack_vector: Debug Port Exploitation (key extraction, code execution)
defense_vectors.layer1: Physical: Secure MCU packaging (potting, fused case); tamper-evident seals
defense_vectors.layer2: Port Access: Debug ports (JTAG/SWD) disabled via fuses in production; readable fuse state in Secure Boot ROM
defense_vectors.layer3: Software: Secure boot enforces debug-disable before loading App; one-time unlock via HMAC challenge (dev/mfg only)
defense_vectors.layer4: Verification: Bootloader confirms debug-disable state; attestation quotes PCR values (including boot config)
defense_vectors.layer5: Audit: All debug unlock requests logged; unlock tokens tied to HWID + timestamp
defense_vectors.coverage: Hardware + software layering; debug fully disabled in production
defense_vectors.notes: TARA-4 threat; requires secure provisioning at manufacturing and tight access control at service

defense_vectors.layer1: Firewall: Rate limiting per message type; reject out-of-order messages
defense_vectors.layer2: Protocol: SecOC (AUTOSAR) enforces CMAC-AES-128 on safety-critical frames; receiver validates MAC + freshness
defense_vectors.layer3: Key Management: Per-ECU SecOC keys derived from secure root; keys rotated on firmware OTA
defense_vectors.layer4: Acceptance Criteria: ECU application logic validates message ranges and timing; rejects anomalies
defense_vectors.layer5: Logging: All SecOC failures logged (bad MAC, replay attempt); triggers diagnostic alert
defense_vectors.coverage: MAC-based authentication + freshness + acceptance criteria prevents spoofing
defense_vectors.notes: TARA-3 threat (safety-critical); SecOC mandatory for steering, braking, ESC control

defense_vectors.layer1: Shielding: Faraday cage (metal enclosure) isolates high-power nodes; EMI suppression
defense_vectors.layer2: Masking: Cryptographic library implements side-channel resistant AES (constant-time, masked multiplications)
defense_vectors.layer3: Noise: Power supply decoupling (large capacitors); clock jitter injection (if implemented)
defense_vectors.layer4: Detection: Anomaly detection on power consumption; triggers watchdog reset on detected glitch
defense_vectors.layer5: Audit: Side-channel test suite (automated DPA resistance validation) runs during secure boot
defense_vectors.coverage: Hardware + algorithmic defenses; detection as failsafe
defense_vectors.notes: TARA-3 threat (key extraction risk); HSM-based key storage isolates sensitive ops

defense_vectors.attack_vector: OTA Rollback Attack (downgrade to vulnerable firmware)
defense_vectors.layer1: Server-side: Minimum firmware version enforced server-side; client version verification in OTA metadata
defense_vectors.layer2: Transport: OTA metadata signed by OEM (separate signing key from firmware key); TLS 1.3 ensures freshness
defense_vectors.layer3: Device: Bootloader compares OTA image version against monotonic counter in secure NVM; rejects if version < current
defense_vectors.layer4: Secure NVM: Version counter stored in OTP fuse or secure flash (encrypted, HMAC-protected); incremented on successful boot
defense_vectors.layer5: Attestation: Device reports current version + PCR values; server validates via TPM quote verification
defense_vectors.coverage: Server-side + device-side anti-rollback; monotonic counter as enforcement
defense_vectors.notes: TARA-3 threat; requires secure NVM and tight boot sequence verification
